questions.prompt: How do you build a ChatGPT workspace agent, according to OpenAI's cookbook?

options.text: You describe the workflow to a conversational builder, which drafts the agent.
options.explanation: Right. The builder drafts the name, instructions and connected apps for you to review.

options.text: You write the agent in Python and upload it to ChatGPT.
options.explanation: The cookbook builds the agent without code, through the conversational builder.

options.text: You fill in a fixed form with a name and a prompt, and it is ready.
options.explanation: The cookbook shows the team building it themselves in ChatGPT.

questions.prompt: What does Anthropic's Console do for Claude Managed Agents?

options.text: It runs agents in production with no code at any step.
options.explanation: The docs say you then reference the agent from your code to run sessions.

options.text: It lets you set up and test an agent visually, then shows the API request to use in code.
options.explanation: Right. Setup and testing need no code; running it in your product does.

options.text: It is a billing page where you set a spending cap for each agent.
options.explanation: The Console page describes a visual tool for creating and configuring agents.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's migration guide warn about moving off Agent Builder?

options.text: Every workflow moves over automatically with no changes.
options.explanation: The guide says the opposite: it doesn't guarantee every behaviour transfers unchanged.

options.text: Workflows can't be exported at all, so they must be rebuilt from memory.
options.explanation: The guide describes exporting the workflow as Agents SDK code.

options.text: The export doesn't convert the graph or guarantee every behaviour transfers unchanged.
options.explanation: Right. That is why keeping your own tests and expected results outside the tool matters.
